title: Jamboard notes — devexp innovation lanes & quickstart canary — 2025-08-29
content:
Context: Weekly devexp sync — informal jamboard session to capture micro-ideas, canary quickstart run notes, and spike proposals. Attendees: Maya (owner), Diego, Sara, Tomás, Anya + 2 drop-ins from product-hosted-api. Duration: 45m.

Goals for this session:
- Rapid capture of 3 small experiments that could improve quickstart completion/conversion.
- Decide on a canary quickstart flow for SDK v0.19 that reduces friction for first-run tokens.
- Surface any docs/samples blockers that need immediate triage.

Top-line outcome: agreed to run two 2-week experiments (sample garden pruning + ephemeral local runner) and a canary quickstart update that adds a guided first-run telemetry opt-in and one-click example.

Notes from the jamboard (raw bullets / shorthand):
- Problem statement: onboarding drop-off at "first API call" stage. telemetry shows ~63% success to first completion; target 85% by EoQ. (Source: quickstarts-dashboard, sampled events)
- Hypothesis A (sample garden pruning): reduce cognitive load by surfacing 3 opinionated example projects (chat, doc-qa, embeddings-search) instead of 12. Idea: highlight a single "copy-and-run" example per language.
- Hypothesis B (ephemeral local runner): provide a tiny CLI wrapper that spins up a container with configured env vars (REDWOOD_API_KEY env masked) so users avoid local env config mistakes. Could be implemented as a docker-compose snippet + small node script.
- Hypothesis C (guided first-run): change quickstart flow to include an in-console guided checklist + telemetry opt-in. Add explicit failure messages for common errors (401, connection refused, incompatible node version).
- Quick win: add explicit debug snippet for "missing permissions" in Python SDK docs (common support topic).
- Accessibility note: make copy snippets keyboard-focusable in sample site; current behavior loses focus after copy.

Decisions made:
- Run Hypothesis A and C in parallel for 2 weeks. A leads PR in samples repo, C leads PR in docs + console. Hypothesis B is deferred to spike after initial results because it touches infra.
- Canary quickstart update to be shipped behind feature flag "canary_quickstart_v1" so we can route 10% of new signups. Product agreed to flag gating.
- Telemetry opt-in copy: "Help us improve quickstarts — anonymous usage data only (no prompt contents)." Legal signoff required (Anya).

Action items (owner — due):
- Diego Morales — create trimmed sample garden branch with 3 canonical examples + README (due 2025-09-05) — LINK: github.com/redwood-inference/samples#trimmed-garden (placeholder).
- Sara Lin — draft docs copy for guided first-run + error message patterns; post to Confluence for review (due 2025-09-02).
- Tomás Rivera — add console feature flag scaffolding and telemetry opt-in UI mock; coordinate with product-hosted-api (due 2025-09-04).
- Maya Kapoor — run quick audit of existing clipboard copy behaviour on sample site across browsers; open issue for a11y fix (due 2025-09-03).
- Anya Patel — legal review on telemetry language and privacy phrasing (due 2025-09-08).

Blockers and risks:
- Legal signoff on telemetry copy may delay the canary ramp. Contingency: ship the UI disabled by default and enable only after approval.
- Infra constraints for ephemeral runner spike: need SRE alignment for any publicly runnable container images. Must coordinate with infra/sre.
- Metrics tracking: ensure quickstarts-dashboard has event for "canary_quickstart_v1" assignment so we can measure conversion. Product to add instrumentation ticket.

Metrics / telemetry to watch during the canary:
- First-run success rate (goal: move from 63% -> 75% within 2 weeks for canary cohort).
- Time-to-first-token (median).
- Help/Support inquiries referencing quickstart — expect to drop support volume for common errors.

Follow-ups / parking lot:
- Spike for ephemeral local runner (Hypothesis B) — scope a 1-week spike to prototype a tiny CLI; move to backlog if infra gating is heavy.
- Internationalization: quickstarts currently EN-only; discuss prioritization once canary shows lift.
- SDK telemetry opt-ins: coordinate with eng-serving-runtime for minimal instrumentation.

Meeting artifacts & links:
- Jamboard board (live, editable) — https://jamboard.google.com/d/1EXAMPLEJAM
- Draft trimmed-samples branch (start after Diego forks) — https://github.com/redwood-inference/samples
- Confluence space for canary plan — https://confluence.redwood.com/display/DEVEXP/Canary-Quickstart-Plan

Next check-in: informal demo of sample garden prototypes + review of docs copy on 2025-09-09 (15m).

Notes to self (Maya): keep the first-run troubleshooting section tiny and example-driven. If legal pushes back strongly, show alternative privacy-preserving wording suggested by Anya.

Unresolved questions:
- Should the canary force a short interactive tour in console, or use an unobtrusive banner? (defer decision to product-hosted-api after mockups)
- Where to store the ephemeral runner images if we go forward — internal registry vs public. Infra input required.

Raw brainstorm fragments (kept for traceability):
- "one-click run on Replit-style ephemeral environment" — high lift but great for teaching.
- "sample badges: beginner / advanced / production" on sample list to reduce choice anxiety.
- "quickstart telemetry: only send 'success/failure' + duration, no prompt text" — legal liked this as a fallback.

End of notes.
